Bug_Title: ICAST: Integral value cast to double and then passed to Math.ceil (ICAST_INT_CAST_TO_DOUBLE_PASSED_TO_CEIL)
Bug_Details:
This code converts an integral value (e.g., int or long)
to a double precision
floating point number and then
passing the result to the Math.ceil() function, which rounds a double to
the next higher integer value. This operation should always be a no-op,
since converting an integer to a double should give a number with no fractional part.
It is likely that the operation that generated the value to be passed
to Math.ceil was intended to be performed using double precision
floating point arithmetic.
Bug_Explanation: This Java code demonstrates the bug where an integral value is cast to double and then passed to the Math.ceil() function. As the value has no fractional part, this operation should always be a no-op. However, since Java performs widening primitive conversion (int to double), the value is implicitly rounded to a double. Hence, Math.ceil() returns the same value.
Trigger_Explanation: The test triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with integral values (5, 55) and expects the result to be the same as the input because Math.ceil operation does not change the integer values. However, since the input is cast to double before passing to Math.ceil, the test fails because the result is not as expected.

Therefore, the Math.ceil function is not necessary in this case and can be considered a bug.
